question: A pole is standing on the top of a house. The height of the house is 25 metres. The angle of elevation of the top of the house from point P is 45° and the angle of elevation of the top of pole from P is 60°. Point P is on the ground level. What is the height of the pole (in metres)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

From the house triangle (45°): Base = Height ÷ tan(45°) = 25 ÷ 1 = 25 m.

From the total height triangle (60°): Total Height = Base × tan(60°) = 25√3 m.

Height of pole = Total Height − Height of House.

Height of pole = 25√3 − 25 = 25(√3 − 1) m.

**∴ The correct answer is 25(√3−1) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height of the house = 25 m

Angle of elevation to top of house = 45°

Angle of elevation to top of pole = 60°

**Formula Used:**

tan(θ) = Perpendicular ÷ Base

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the base distance be x and height of the pole be h.

⇒ For the lower right-angled triangle formed by the house:

⇒ tan(45°) = 25 ÷ x

⇒ 1 = 25 ÷ x

⇒ x = 25 m

⇒ For the larger right-angled triangle formed by the pole and house:

⇒ tan(60°) = (25 + h) ÷ x

⇒ √3 = (25 + h) ÷ 25

⇒ 25√3 = 25 + h

⇒ h = 25√3 − 25

⇒ h = 25(√3 − 1) m

**∴ The correct answer is 25(√3−1) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when viewing an object located above the horizontal level.

Key Trigonometric Ratios

For height and distance problems, the tangent ratios are most commonly used: tan(30°) = 1/√3, tan(45°) = 1, tan(60°) = √3.

Complementary Angles Trick

If the angles of elevation of the top of a tower from two points at distances a and b from its base are complementary, the height of the tower is √(a × b).
